c10_live.first.02.speaker: shaw
c10_live.first.02.text: Field lights following. We can match that.
c10_live.first.02.synthesis_text: Field lights following. We can match that.
c10_live.first.02.previous_text: First street ready. Second street ready. Look at the harbor, Steve.
c10_live.first.02.next_text: I called Orchard. When a fresh Pier flash answered Orchard’s change, I released Shaw’s lights. A reply, made live, that nobody could have recorded.

c1_dinner.family.lead.05.speaker: mateo
c1_dinner.family.lead.05.text: Funny. Lyle Boone hasn’t missed one of the Little League games I coach since June either.
c1_dinner.family.lead.05.synthesis_text: Funny. Lyle Boone hasn’t missed one of the Little League games I coach since June either.
c1_dinner.family.lead.05.previous_text: She called my show every episode to fix my tide tables. The last call was May seventeenth.
c1_dinner.family.lead.05.next_text: Eat before it gets cold, Steve. Then tell us what is troubling you.

c1_dinner.out.03.speaker: carmen
c1_dinner.out.03.text: Next Sunday, Steve. The plate will be warm.
c1_dinner.out.03.synthesis_text: Next Sunday, Steve. The plate will be warm.
c1_dinner.out.03.previous_text: I’m tired. Let’s go home, sleepyhead.

c1_flat.compare.02.speaker: steve
c1_flat.compare.02.text: And Nora... lines up too. The breath. The little click before “morning.”
c1_flat.compare.02.synthesis_text: And Nora... lines up too. The breath. The little click before “morning.”
c1_flat.compare.02.previous_text: Twelve seconds, both days. Dad’s recorder runs true.
c1_flat.compare.02.next_text: Nobody says a sentence the same way twice. I spent twelve years listening for exactly that.

c2_ship.in.03.speaker: steve
c2_ship.in.03.text: I’d prefer the exit. Does that come with music too?
c2_ship.in.03.synthesis_text: I’d prefer the exit. Does that come with music too?
c2_ship.in.03.previous_text: Would peaceful human hold music assist your experience?
c2_ship.in.03.next_text: “You are the author of your own story.” This is from a human book. Is it helping?

c2_ship.intake.01.speaker: steve
c2_ship.intake.01.text: Come on, Admiral. You never missed this one.
c2_ship.intake.01.synthesis_text: Come on, Admiral. You never missed this one.
c2_ship.intake.01.previous_text: The tunnel’s flooding. The underwater speakers still work... I fixed them, the day I met her.
c2_ship.intake.01.next_text: Nora’s real whistle, through the speakers I fixed the day we met. Admiral came down through the dark and dragged me to the surface.

c4_escape.out.01.speaker: rook_copy
c4_escape.out.01.text: All units. Steve Mercer, wanted for the abduction of Nora Reyes. And scan Calder tonight. The signing is in six days.
c4_escape.out.01.synthesis_text: All units. Steve Mercer, wanted for the abduction of Nora Reyes. And scan Calder tonight. The signing is in six days.
c4_escape.out.01.previous_text: Now I was in a ditch in the Coast Range with Dad’s recorder, a stolen radio and no plan. And the radio was still talking.
c4_escape.out.01.next_text: Kidnapping Nora. They took her, and I’m the one on the poster. I have to keep moving.

c4_safe.screens.01.speaker: steve
c4_safe.screens.01.text: Adrian Rook, asleep in bed 41B. Both governments’ seals on the transfer. And an empty bed waiting for President Ward on signing day.
c4_safe.screens.01.synthesis_text: Adrian Rook, asleep in bed 41B. Both governments’ seals on the transfer. And an empty bed waiting for President Ward on signing day.
c4_safe.screens.01.previous_text: While he was singing, his office door was open.

c5_shack.in.06.speaker: luis
c5_shack.in.06.text: I’ve heard the bay sing since I was a boy. Your father was the only one who ever asked me what it sounded like.
c5_shack.in.06.synthesis_text: I’ve heard the bay sing since I was a boy. Your father was the only one who ever asked me what it sounded like.
c5_shack.in.06.previous_text: Nora has been gone since Tuesday night. Carmen hasn’t slept. And I have known you since you were nine years old.
c5_shack.in.06.next_text: Forty-five years of kitchen-table notes. Every morning, one of them left the other one a note.

c5_shack.rig.lead.01.speaker: steve
c5_shack.rig.lead.01.text: Dad’s receiver. Dead battery, and the dial’s slipped since he last used it.
c5_shack.rig.lead.01.synthesis_text: Dad’s receiver. Dead battery, and the dial’s slipped since he last used it.
c5_shack.rig.lead.01.previous_text: Dad’s “Done” answers Mom’s March 2 slip: he filed their tape between the Coltrane and the weather carts. The good stuff is the KBWR record library. Mom hid her notebook at my old station.
c5_shack.rig.lead.01.next_text: Every set has a rating card, Dad said. Read it before you plug anything in.

c5_station.automation.lead.01.speaker: steve
c5_station.automation.lead.01.text: AutoRick’s console. I wrote half these carts myself.
c5_station.automation.lead.01.synthesis_text: AutoRick’s console. I wrote half these carts myself.
c5_station.automation.lead.01.previous_text: Two fellas. Somebody else is breathing in here.
c5_station.automation.lead.01.next_text: I built this schedule before they replaced me with it. And the door still opens for my voice.

c7_gate.out.05.speaker: stephen
c7_gate.out.05.text: So we watch the hatch. I’m very good at being looked at.
c7_gate.out.05.synthesis_text: So we watch the hatch. I’m very good at being looked at.
c7_gate.out.05.previous_text: If they swap her, it happens between the hatch and the podium.
c7_gate.out.05.next_text: In the fog between the antennas, an old woman was walking a dog. Mrs. Penhallow. Miles from her pier, again.

c7_gate.truck.lead.02.speaker: shaw
c7_gate.truck.lead.02.text: The back fence failed the check. Sound crosses three hundred and forty meters in a second, and the fence is a hundred and seventy meters out. Tell me what it actually heard.
c7_gate.truck.lead.02.synthesis_text: The back fence failed the check. Sound crosses three hundred and forty meters in a second, and the fence is a hundred and seventy meters out. Tell me what it actually heard.
c7_gate.truck.lead.02.previous_text: Evelyn Shaw. I ran the sound stage for Meridian, back when it had a budget. Stay off the cables.
c7_gate.truck.lead.02.next_text: Half a second. Good ears. Who taught you?

c7_swap.recap.03.speaker: steve
c7_swap.recap.03.text: Rook’s copy slipped away into the fog. Before he went, he asked me one thing.
c7_swap.recap.03.synthesis_text: Rook’s copy slipped away into the fog. Before he went, he asked me one thing.
c7_swap.recap.03.previous_text: Iris told me later that the tone pulled at her too. She held on to June’s sleeve and counted Sunday dinners until it passed.
c7_swap.recap.03.next_text: Is he awake? The other one?

c8_lab.in.05.speaker: wen
c8_lab.in.05.text: Mine fooled six. And a premier.
c8_lab.in.05.synthesis_text: Mine fooled six. And a premier.
c8_lab.in.05.next_text: Help me put her pages back in order.

c8_lab.lastpage.find.speaker: steve
c8_lab.lastpage.find.text: Mom’s last page is Dad’s Reel 11: two joined tones rising, 220 to 330, a half-second gap, then a long 165, lower than both. Her margin says it repeats after the low note. It’s a language, and nobody on Earth can read it.
c8_lab.lastpage.find.synthesis_text: Mom’s last page is Dad’s Reel 11: two joined tones rising, 220 to 330, a half-second gap, then a long 165, lower than both. Her margin says it repeats after the low note. It’s a language, and nobody on Earth can read it.
c8_lab.lastpage.find.next_text: Two countries faked two tests and broadcast them on open radio. Something out there was listening, and it came. Mom heard the proof in the bay.

c9_wake.agnes.find.speaker: steve
c9_wake.agnes.find.text: Mrs. Penhallow’s glasses, from the middle tray. Her bed tag says she’s been asleep in here for three years. So who has been selling me bait?
c9_wake.agnes.find.synthesis_text: Mrs. Penhallow’s glasses, from the middle tray. Her bed tag says she’s been asleep in here for three years. So who has been selling me bait?
c9_wake.agnes.find.previous_text: My glasses. Has somebody changed the price of bait while I was gone?
c9_wake.agnes.find.next_text: Dad woke to his call sign, Mom to her lullaby, Adrian Rook to June’s voice, and Mrs. Penhallow to her reading glasses.
